p: A bland first contact put you among the interchangeable suppliers.
In through the wrong door: you had to justify your price later.
q: Pain badly quantified: the client never saw what the status quo cost.
With no decision-maker identified, the budget was set without you.
pr: A generic demo: the client compared features, so prices.
Your presentation never tied the solution to a measurable gain.
n: A concession for nothing: the discount became the benchmark.
You negotiated against yourself before the client even asked.
c: The close reopened the price: the last points cost dear.
A signature wrung out at the last minute gets paid for in discount.

intro.title: You are an Account Executive
intro.body: Each game is a B2B deal run in 5 stages, from prospecting to closing. One decision per stage.

intro.title: Three answers, one senior instinct
intro.body: Senior instinct, it'll do or unforced error: each choice warms or cools the deal. At 70, it signs.

intro.title: Sign, and at the right price
intro.body: The amount signed depends on your answers, above all in negotiation and closing. Your revenue is what you protect.

signed: That one goes in the forecast.
Clean. Tell the team about this deal on Monday.
Signed before quarter end. Thank you.
Good cycle. Keep the notes, they'll come in handy.
The client signed without a chaser. That's rare.
Nice. Start thinking about the renewal now.
Nothing to add. That's rare too.
Well played. Finance might finally smile.
delayed: We'll talk on Monday.
Smells like it slips to next quarter.
Not lost. Not won either.
It stays in the pipeline, not the forecast.
A decision-maker is missing somewhere. Find them.
Keep the contact warm, it may come back.
"We'll get back to you." We know that one.
One stage got stuck. Which one, do you think?
signedLow: Signed, yes. But look at what's left of the value.
The client signed. Finance will look at the discount.
Good deal for the client. For us, not so much.
You won the deal and lost the margin. Replay it.
lost: Shall we debrief together?
"Call me in January," as the client would say.
It happens. Look at where it tipped.
Lost, but now you know why.
The competitor was there at the right time. You weren't.
These aren't lost at the close. They're lost before.
Note what you'd do differently. Then replay.
A deal lost early costs less than one lost late.

sales-vp.role: One quarter. Five decisions. One team.

fc: A number badly defended: the board set yours for you.
The forecast slipped, and trust went with it.
pp: Undated deals kept in the pipe: the team worked on thin air.
The pipe was never cut: the quarter was decided too late.
co: Generic coaching: the AE made the same mistake on the next deal.
The moment to coach passed without the sentence that changes everything.
rc: A comfort hire: the team gained a head, not a strength.
The team's balance gave way: the number rested on too few people.
ar: A trade-off put off: leadership decided without you.
You said yes where you had to say no: the team paid for it.

intro.title: You are VP · Head of Sales
intro.body: Each game is a quarter. Five decisions: forecast, pipe review, coaching, hiring, trade-offs.

intro.title: Three answers, one VP instinct
intro.body: VP instinct, it'll do or management error: each choice warms or cools the quarter. At 70, it holds.

intro.title: Protect your team's revenue
intro.body: Protected revenue depends on your answers, above all in hiring and trade-offs. Your revenue is what the team keeps.

signed: Quarter held. I'll show the board as is.
Clean. Your team knows where it's going.
The number is there, and so is the team. Thank you.
Good quarter. Write down what you did, it'll come in handy.
Not one surprise in the forecast. That's rare.
You made the call at the right time. Keep going.
Nothing to add. That's rare too.
The CFO smiled. I'm noting the date.
delayed: We'll talk on Monday.
The number is slipping. I want to know where.
Not missed. Not held either.
I'll keep your forecast, but I'll reread it.
A decision was missing somewhere. Which one?
The board will have questions. Prepare them.
"It lands next quarter." We know that one.
Your team ran. In which direction?
signedLow: Held, yes. But look at what it cost.
The quarter goes through. The team paid for it.
Fine for this quarter. Next one, not so much.
You held the number and lost margin. Replay.
lost: Shall we take stock together?
Your team is at risk. So am I, then.
It happens. Look at where it tipped.
Lost, but now you know why.
The problem wasn't the market. Look elsewhere.
Quarters are lost early, not at month end.
Note what you'd do differently. Then replay.
A team can be rebuilt. Start on Monday.

sales-sdr.role: Three minutes. Someone who asked for nothing.

ci: The wrong contact: the meeting happened, not with the one who decides.
An account picked for no reason of the moment: interest faded before the meeting.
ac: An opener about you, not him: he said yes to be polite.
The first fifteen seconds were lost: the prospect is half-listening.
so: The objection was dodged, not handled: it will come back at the AE.
The gatekeeper was forced: the meeting starts with a bad impression.
qu: No stakes, no decision-maker, no date: the AE starts from scratch.
Surface qualification: the estimated deal melted at the first exchange.
re: An incomplete handover: the AE asked the same questions again.
The context stayed in your head: the prospect had to repeat everything.

intro.title: You are an SDR · BDR
intro.body: Each game is an account to open. Five decisions: targeting, opener, gatekeepers and objections, qualification, handover.

intro.title: Three answers, one SDR instinct
intro.body: SDR instinct, it'll do or prospecting error: each choice warms or cools the account. At 70, the meeting is qualified.

intro.title: Build pipe for your AE
intro.body: The pipe you build depends on your answers, above all in qualification and handover. A badly qualified meeting is worth little.

signed: Clean meeting. The AE had nothing to ask again.
Well targeted, well qualified. That's the job.
The AE thanked me. That doesn't happen every day.
You opened an account others had given up on.
Good opener. Keep it, you'll use it again.
Stakes, decision-maker, date: it's all there.
That meeting will hold. I'm noting it.
Three minutes well spent. Keep going.
delayed: Meeting booked, but I wouldn't bet on it.
The decision-maker is missing. Or the date. Or both.
The AE will have to requalify everything.
Not missed. Not solid either.
Did he say yes just to hang up faster?
Reread your notes before the handover.
A shaky meeting is a no-show waiting to happen.
The account is open. Halfway.
signedLow: Qualified, yes. But the deal shrank on the way.
Meeting held, stakes cut down. Look where.
The AE has the meeting. Not all the context.
Good meeting, small pipe. Replay qualification.
lost: Shall we take stock together?
Hung up. Look at which sentence.
It happens. The next call is in two minutes.
The "no" was workable. Find where.
Wrong target or wrong opener? Replay.
Note what you'd say differently. Then call back.
An account lost on the first call isn't lost for good.
Accounts are lost in the first fifteen seconds.
